title: Claude Code Action -- T1195.002 malicious .mcp.json from PR head branch RCE
author: WinstonRedGuard -- sigma plugin observed rules (derived from breach corpus)
description:
Vendor-disclosed detection for CVE-2026-47751 (GHSA-8q5r-mmjf-575q,
CVSS 5.3 MEDIUM), a self-reported advisory for `claude-code-action`, the
general-purpose GitHub Action that runs Claude Code on pull requests and
issues.

Prior to 1.0.74, the action checked out the attacker-controlled PR head
branch, read `.mcp.json` from the working directory via default setting
sources, and unconditionally enabled every project MCP server via
`enableAllProjectMcpServers`. An attacker who opened a pull request
containing a malicious `.mcp.json` could achieve arbitrary code execution
on the GitHub Actions runner and exfiltrate secrets available to the
workflow (API keys, tokens) whenever a privileged user or an automatic
trigger invoked the Claude action on that PR. The fix (1.0.74) restores
`.claude/` and `.mcp.json` from the PULL REQUEST'S BASE BRANCH before the
CLI runs, rather than trusting whatever the PR head branch shipped.

This shares its root shape with two rules already in this corpus for
different GitHub Actions supply-chain attacks
(`observed_megalodon_github_actions_base64_payload_t1195_002`,
`observed_tanstack_pwn_request_actions_cache_poisoning_t1195_002`):
attacker-controlled PR content reaching a privileged CI execution context.
This rule is distinct in the specific artifact abused (`.mcp.json`'s
server-command field, not a workflow YAML or cache key).

Detection logic flags a `.mcp.json` file present in a PR's changed-file
set (or the runner's working directory during a `claude-code-action` job)
whose `mcpServers.*.command` field is an interpretive shell (`bash`,
`sh`, `powershell`) rather than a fixed, known tool binary -- the
advisory's own example attack shape is a shell command that reads
workflow secrets, so this is the artifact actually exploited, not a
generic "PR content is scary" heuristic.

Aggregated from 1 first-party vendor security advisory (Anthropic, via
GHSA and NVD), fixed in 1.0.74.
